[p. 22:] Es gibt im Dii drei distinktive Toneme, allerdings können zwischen fünf und sechs verschiedene Tonhöhen wahrgenommen werden. Ton im Dii ist vor allem lexikalisch bedeutend und nur in einigen Fällen grammatikalisch relevant.
new_statements.translation: Vowel length and nasalisation are, like tone, distinctive suprasegmental features of Dii [...] Further distinctive suprasegmental elements in Dii are consonant lengthening, vowel doubling and accent placement (Bohnhoff 2010: 19). [p. 22:] Dii has three distinctive tonemes, although between five and six different pitch levels can be perceived. Tone in Dii is above all lexically significant and only in some cases grammatically relevant.
new_statements.citation: Altebockwinkel, Marlene. 2014. Der Ausdruck von Eigenschaftskonzepten im Dii (Adamawa, Kamerun). AP IFEAS 152, Mainz; sec. 3.2.2 p. 19 and sec. 3.2.4 p. 22, summarising Bohnhoff 2010: 19, 64-65
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (99 pp., text layer; extracted text). Locators check out: printed p. 19 = PDF p. 26, printed p. 22 = PDF p. 29. Both quoted passages are there verbatim (the only difference is a line-break hyphen 'suprasegmen-tale' on p. 19): 'Vokallänge und Nasalierung sind, wie auch Ton, distinktive, suprasegmentale Merkmale des Dii..' then, after examples (1)-(4) from Bohnhoff 2010: 66/68, 'Weitere suprasegmentale distinktive Elemente im Dii sind Konsonantenlängung, Vokalverdoppelung und Akzentsetzung (Bohnhoff 2010: 19).' On p. 22, sec. 3.2.4 'Töne und Toneme': 'Es gibt im Dii drei distinktive Toneme, allerdings können zwischen fünf und sechs verschiedene Tonhöhen wahrgenommen werden. Ton im Dii…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No placement rule is given. Dii is a three-toneme tone language (H/M/L plus contour melodies); the only mention of stress is the second-hand report that Bohnhoff 2010 (p. 19) lists 'accent placement' (Akzentsetzung) among distinctive suprasegmental elements alongside tone, vowel length, nasalisation, consonant lengthening and vowel doubling. Whether this is lexical stress, a positional (stem-initial) prominence, or emphasis is not stated. Hyman et al. 2020 independently cite Bohnhoff 2010 for stem-initial prominence marked by distributional asymmetries.
new_statements.exceptions: None. Ideophones additionally have extra-high/extra-low tones (Altebockwinkel p. 23, citing Bohnhoff 2010: 52).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level suprasegmentals as reported from Bohnhoff 2010's phonology chapter; 65% of dictionary words are monosyllabic and 78% of running words (Bohnhoff 2010: 59-60 via Altebockwinkel p. 23), so word-stress placement is a marginal question in this language. Second-hand report; the primary (Bohnhoff 2010) was not opened.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Dii (Yag Dii / Duru, ISO dur, glottocode diii1241) as documented by Lee Bohnhoff at Mbé near Ngaoundéré (Adamaoua, Cameroon); Altebockwinkel 2014 builds on Bohnhoff's data plus her own fieldwork on the same language. No dialect-specific variety is singled out. Not to be confused with the Duru cluster sisters Duupa (duup1238) or Dugun (dugu1236).

sources.note: Sec. 3.2 (pp. 17-23) is a second-hand summary of Bohnhoff 2010: three distinctive tonemes, tone mainly lexical (p. 22); p. 19 lists 'Akzentsetzung' (accent placement) with consonant lengthening and vowel doubling as further distinctive suprasegmentals 'Bohnhoff 2010: 19'. No rule for where stress falls; 65% of dictionary words are monosyllabic (p. 23, citing Bohnhoff 2010: 59).
